shared_upstream_stages: oil and natural-gas extraction and processing
steam cracking, fluid catalytic cracking, dehydrogenation, or aromatic production
compounding with stabilizers, pigments, fillers, plasticizers, flame retardants, or processing aids
conversion by extrusion, injection molding, blow molding, thermoforming, fiber spinning, casting, foaming, or curing

steps: Steam crack natural-gas liquids or petroleum feedstocks to ethylene.
Oxidize ethylene to ethylene oxide and hydrolyze it to ethylene glycol.
Recover p-xylene from refinery/aromatics streams and oxidize it to purified terephthalic acid (PTA), or convert to dimethyl terephthalate (DMT).
React ethylene glycol with PTA or DMT by esterification/transesterification and melt polycondensation.
Use solid-state polymerization when higher molecular weight is required; dry and pelletize resin.
Convert to bottles/trays by injection-stretch-blow molding or thermoforming, or spin into polyester fiber.
Steam crack natural-gas liquids or petroleum feedstocks to ethylene.
Purify ethylene and polymerize it using low-pressure catalytic slurry, solution, or gas-phase processes.
Separate unreacted monomer, stabilize, extrude, cool, and pelletize resin.
Blow mold bottles, extrude pipe/sheet/film, or injection mold durable parts.
Produce and purify ethylene through the same upstream routes used for HDPE.
For LDPE, use high-pressure free-radical polymerization in tubular or autoclave reactors.
For LLDPE, use lower-pressure catalytic copolymerization of ethylene with butene, hexene, or octene in solution, slurry, or gas phase.
Recover monomer, add stabilizers/slip/antiblock agents as needed, pelletize, and extrude into film or coatings.
pathways.process_note: The cited GREET-based report assigns more polymerization energy to LDPE than HDPE because LDPE uses high-pressure reactors.

steps: Source propylene as a steam-cracker or fluid-catalytic-cracker coproduct, or make it by propane dehydrogenation above 500 C.
Purify propylene and polymerize it catalytically in bulk, slurry, solution, or gas-phase reactors.
Remove residual monomer/catalyst, compound with stabilizers and fillers, extrude, cool, and pelletize.
Convert by injection molding, film extrusion/orientation, melt-blown/spun-bond fiber, or thermoforming.
Electrolyze purified brine in a chlor-alkali plant to chlorine, caustic soda, and hydrogen.
React ethylene and chlorine to ethylene dichloride (EDC); recover HCl through oxychlorination loops.
Crack EDC to vinyl chloride monomer (VCM) and purify the monomer.
Polymerize VCM by suspension, emulsion, or bulk polymerization; strip residual monomer, dewater, dry, and classify resin.
Compound rigid PVC with stabilizers/fillers or flexible PVC with plasticizers, then extrude, calender, mold, or coat.
pathways.regional_note: The ethylene/EDC route dominates the cited U.S. model; coal/calcium-carbide acetylene routes have been more important in China.

primary_inputs: pentane or another blowing agent for EPS
steps: Alkylate benzene with ethylene to ethylbenzene and dehydrogenate it to styrene.
Polymerize styrene by mass, suspension, or emulsion methods; add rubber phase for high-impact polystyrene.
For EPS, impregnate beads with blowing agent, pre-expand with steam, age, and mold with additional steam.
For solid PS, extrude or injection mold; for extruded foam, combine melt with blowing agent.
Produce propylene oxide/ethylene oxide and initiate ring-opening reactions to make polyether polyols, or esterify acids and glycols for polyester polyols.
Produce aniline-derived MDI or toluene-derived TDI through nitration/hydrogenation and phosgenation routes.
Meter polyol, isocyanate, catalyst, surfactant, additives, and water/physical blowing agent into a reactive mix.
Foam, cast, spray, coat, or mold while urethane linkages form and the product cures.
Make acrylonitrile by catalytic ammoxidation of propylene; source butadiene and styrene from petrochemical routes.
For SAN, copolymerize styrene and acrylonitrile; for ABS, graft SAN phases onto polybutadiene rubber by emulsion or mass polymerization and compound.
For PMMA, make methyl methacrylate and polymerize it by bulk, suspension, solution, or emulsion routes.
For acrylic fiber, polymerize acrylonitrile-rich copolymers, dissolve, spin, wash, draw, and dry fibers.

primary_inputs: phosgene or diphenyl carbonate for PC
steps: React phenol and acetone to bisphenol A.
Produce polycarbonate by interfacial phosgene chemistry or melt transesterification with diphenyl carbonate, then pelletize.
Produce common epoxy resin by reacting bisphenol A with epichlorohydrin, then formulate with curing agents and fillers.
Mold/extrude PC or apply/cure epoxy as coating, adhesive, composite matrix, or can lining.

primary_inputs: adipic acid and hexamethylenediamine for nylon 6,6
steps: Make caprolactam from cyclohexanone oxime and ring-open/polymerize it to nylon 6, with extraction of residual monomer/oligomer.
For nylon 6,6, make adipic acid and hexamethylenediamine, form nylon salt, and perform melt polycondensation with water removal.
Pelletize for molded products or melt-spin into fibers, then draw, finish, and textile-process.
Make fluorinated monomers through halogen chemistry.
Polymerize in suspension, emulsion, or other controlled systems; some historical and current routes use nonpolymer PFAS processing aids.
Recover, wash, dry, sinter, extrude, coat, or fabricate high-performance articles.
Manage residuals, air/water emissions, and end-of-life because persistent nonpolymer PFAS may be associated with production and processing.

manufacturing_water_rule: A process flow identifies where water can enter; it is not a quantitative coefficient. Quantitative values belong only in water-intensities.json with boundary, region, year, and source.
